primary_source_citation.title: NASA Robotics Alliance Project Technical Reference: Autonomous Robotics Architecture: Sense -> Plan -> Act Loop

1.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: A true robot closes the Sense-Plan-Act feedback loop autonomously rather than relying purely on open-loop remote control.
core_mechanism_bullets: 1. SENSE (Perception & Telemetry): Ultrasonic time-of-flight, LIDAR, optical wheel encoders, IMU gyroscopes, and limit switches measure world state.
2. PLAN (Microcontroller Decision Logic): State machines and PID feedback controllers compute error (Target minus Measured) 50 to 1,000 times per second.
3. ACT (Mechanical Power Conversion): DC gearmotors, hobby servos, stepper motors, and pneumatic cylinders convert electrical signals into motion.
4. FEEDBACK (Closed-Loop Correction): Encoders verify actual wheel/arm travel and automatically compensate for battery voltage drop or ramp slope.

Step 2: Apply the field rule of thumb (A true robot closes the Sense-Plan-Act feedback loop autonomously rather than relying purely on open-loop remote control.). Step 3: Verify each measurement or checkpoint against NASA Robotics Alliance Project reference criteria and record your findings in your Scout Workbook.

primary_source_citation.title: Carnegie Mellon Robotics Academy & FIRST Technical Reference: Mechanical Power: Gear Ratios, Torque vs. Speed & 6 Degrees of Freedom

2.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Gear Ratio = Driven Teeth / Driver Teeth: a 36-tooth gear driven by a 12-tooth pinion gives 3x torque at 1/3 rotational speed.
core_mechanism_bullets: 1:1 Direct Drive (12T -> 12T): Output speed equals motor RPM and output torque equals motor stall torque; zero mechanical advantage.
1:3 Geared Up for Speed (36T -> 12T): Triples output shaft RPM while cutting available torque to one-third; stalls easily on steep ramps.
3:1 Geared Down for Torque (12T -> 36T): Multiplies lifting and climbing torque 3x (minus ~5% friction) at one-third speed for heavy robot arms.
6 Degrees of Freedom (3 Linear + 3 Rotary): Full 3D workspace requires Surge (X), Sway (Y), Heave (Z) plus Roll, Pitch, and Yaw wrist orientation.

primary_source_citation.title: OSHA Robotics Safety & FIRST Safety Manual Technical Reference: Robotics Shop Safety, LiPo Battery Care & Hazard Prevention

3.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Always remove jewelry, tie back long hair, wear ANSI Z87.1 safety glasses, and disable power before adjusting gears or linkages.
core_mechanism_bullets: Mechanical Pinch & Entanglement Guards: De-energize motors and prop up raised arms on physical safety blocks before reaching near gears, chains, or sprockets.
Lithium-Polymer (LiPo) Battery Safety: Balance-charge inside a fire-resistant LiPo bag; immediately quarantine any puffy, dented, or overheated pack.
Soldering, Fume & Eye Protection: Wear ANSI Z87.1 impact glasses, use a brass tip cleaner and fume extractor, and unplug irons when unattended.
Hardware Emergency Stop (E-Stop): Wire a physical main breaker switch within immediate reach and test software timeout watchdogs before driving.

primary_source_citation.title: NASA Systems Engineering Handbook Technical Reference: Iterative Engineering Design Process & Counselor Review Log

4.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Engineers never erase failed prototypes in the notebook; log the exact failure mode, measurement data, and single variable changed.
core_mechanism_bullets: Stage 1: Problem Constraints & Sketches: Define task geometry, weight/size limits, and sketch at least two competing drivetrain/manipulator concepts.
Stage 2: Subsystem Prototype & Wiring: Build modular chassis and actuator assembly with color-coded wiring (Red V+, Black GND, Yellow/White Signal).
Stage 3: State-Machine Code & Sensor Test: Write clean modular functions with serial telemetry printouts to verify raw sensor thresholds before full speed.
Stage 4: Five-Trial Quantitative Validation: Run 5 consecutive repeatability trials, record cycle times and failure modes, and document design refinements.
